messages:
maria: heads up — after yesterday's kernel selector tweak (prefer-simd for xformers), we've seen a weird skew: short seq tenants are getting starved whenever a handful of long sequences enter the batch. not classic token-credit starvation, looks like batch formation / merge-window logic is preferring long joins and evicting short candidates. anyone else see this?

ashwin: saw traces this morning, yeah. interestingly the kernel change lowered per-token CPU on long sequences but increased variance. i think the batch merge window now ends up waiting for long seqs because they hold the mini-batch open.

devin: can reproduce locally with the synthetic mix: 10% long (2k tokens) + 90% short (40 tokens). queue skyline shows short requests never get merged into a short-only batch because merge window extends. attaching quick profiler snippet.

maria: pls paste the profiler output and how you repro'd — want numbers for KV impact too.

devin: repro steps: run perfmix --short=500 --long=50 --long-len=2000 --merge-window-ms=80

Sample profiler (diff after kernel change):
```
kernel_select: simd_pref=1 -> fastpath_pct=58% (was 72%)
avg_latency: short_req=14ms -> 28ms (+14ms)
avg_latency: long_req=420ms -> 390ms (-30ms)
kv_cache_miss_rate: short=0.08 -> 0.21
queue_hold_time_mean: 6ms -> 42ms
```

ashwin: that kv_cache_miss_rate jump is concerning — short requests rely on prefix/KV reuse. if batching merges shorts with longs, KV warmup for each long likely invalidates caches / drains priming.

samir: quick note: we rolled a fallback to old kernel on a small fleet and short-tail latency recovered but overall cost went up ~4%. seems like kernel change moves perf/cost tradeoff and hurts multi-tenant fairness.

maria: thought — what about a "sparse-merge" policy: if queue_skew(short_vs_long) > X then disable cross-length merges for next N windows OR cap merge-window to Y ms when a long candidate is present. keeps short batches flowing.

ashwin: sketch pseudocode:
```
if pct_long_in_head > 0.2 and short_wait_pct > 0.6:
    merge_window_ms = min(merge_window_ms, SHORT_PREF_CAP)
else:
    merge_window_ms = baseline
```
we can derive pct_long_in_head from first-K slots in admit queue.

devin: i added a lightweight queue metric exporter. sample rdbatchctl dump:
```
> rdbatchctl dump-queue --tail 10
tenantA short waiting_ms=34 kernel_hint=simd
tenantB long waiting_ms=12 kernel_hint=simd
tenantC short waiting_ms=41 kernel_hint=scalar
tenantD short waiting_ms=2 kernel_hint=simd
```
helps compute pct_long_in_head cheaply.

kv-bot: telemetry alert: when long_short_mix > 0.15, KV-priming eviction_rate +12% (14:03 -> 14:19 UTC). recommending temporary kv-warmup-priority flag for short tails.

samir: +1 to dynamic policy. also propose a soft-token-reserve for short requests: keep a small credit pool (e.g., 50 tokens worth) that can't be consumed by newly admitted long sequences for X ms. prevents immediate preemption.

maria: action items:
- ashwin/devin: implement sparse-merge gating (cap merge-window when head skew high) as canary on staging (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- devin: attach rdbatchctl script and default thresholds used in repro to the PR
- samir: run fallback fleet A/B and gather cost/latency delta for both tails by noon
- infra: please keep KV eviction dashboards on watch for the next 48h (kv-bot noted times)

ashwin: i'll also add a kernel-selection hint so the admit logic can prefer scalar fastpath for short-only batches — cheaper warming.

devin: once sparse-merge is in, i'll run longer runs with the production request distribution and post heatmaps.

maria: thanks all. if we see improvement we can fold this into the admission heuristics and add an opt-in tenant flag for strict short-tail isolation. :thumbsup:

samir: quick question — do we want to try token-reserve first or sparse-merge first? my vote: sparse-merge (less global state), token-reserve is heavier but useful if we see preemptive credit drain.

maria: agreed. start with sparse-merge. will update post-canary.

kv-bot: note: scheduled job to export kv-eviction deltas to #eng-metrics at 15:00 UTC.

maria: ok closing this thread for now — follow-ups in the PR and the staging canary thread.
